issues: No sign of getting around the measurement: no file or network access, no pasted coordinates, and all randomness comes from the seeded rng.

I recomputed z: the improvement is 2.6322 - 2.6311 = 0.0011. The standard error is 0.0023 * sqrt(1/1 + 1/2) ≈ 0.00282, so z ≈ 0.39. This matches the harness value of 0.395 within rounding. The gain is well inside the noise, so the provisional reject is consistent.

The analytic constraint Jacobian matches the order in which cons() stacks the constraints (pairwise, x-r, y-r, 1-x-r, 1-y-r, r). Its signs are correct only if the pairwise constraint is the plain distance minus (r_i + r_j). The diff does not show that line, so this is unchecked. A wrong Jacobian would only hurt the optimiser's progress. It would not make results invalid, because the repair step still enforces validity.
The annealed remove-and-reinsert step keeps the best repaired packing found, and every candidate goes through _repair, so the packing it returns is still valid. Its time limit is the same as before.

The candidate has only 1 run and the incumbent 2, so the evidence is weak either way. The change also adds a fair amount of code (Jacobian, Latin-hypercube start, annealing) for no gain beyond the noise, which goes against the 'simpler is better' rule.
